newsitem.title: SYRIA: Egyptian premier in talks with Syrians over peace.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian premier in talks with Syrians over peace.

text.p: Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri had talks with Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam on latest developments of the Middle East peace process, officials said on Wednesday.
They said the talks were held on Tuesday evening in the Syrian Mediterranean city of Latakia, some 320 km (200 miles) north of Damascus.

Ganzouri, accompanied by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Amr Moussa, and Minister of Information, Safawt el-Sherif, is due to meet President Hafez al-Assad at the presidential resort palace in Latakia later on Wednesday to give him a message from President Hosni Mubarak.
The Egyptian information minister said Ganzouri's visit came within the framework of continued coordination and consultations between Syria and Egypt.

The Egyptian team's visit to Syria is the first after a visit by President Mubarak to Washington during which he discussed with President Bill Clinton ways of reviving the Syrian-Israeli peace talks which broke off a year ago.
It also follows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, which was condemned by Arab states.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but the negotiations stalled over the fate of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Syria strongly condemned Netanyahu for refusing to swop occupied Arab lands for peace and refrained for holding any talks with his government, which took over in June.
